instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, I've accepted the museum job. Before I clear my bench, tell me you think I'm ready for it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're thirty. You don't need me to release you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Release and recommendation are different things. You taught me the work; I'm asking whether you think I can do it there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pack your tools. You might want to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hone the blades for use, please, not oil them for storage. I need you sending me to the museum, not preparing for my return.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, we've signed the lease. Pick up your glass, please; I'd like a proper toast to our new home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need my permission to move in with Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lease is signed; that part is finished. I'm asking you to celebrate it. We start with the good wishes, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm pleased for you. I'm still getting used to Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Include Sam by name, Mum. Raise the glass to both of us in our home. Please don't make me supply half the toast myself.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Carry This with Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take half Mum's care-home forms. We are both her children; I can't also be the entire admissions department.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll put you as main contact. You understand these.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Main contact takes the calls; it doesn't mean 'knows everything.' Put your number down. I'll help with anything you can't answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll be ringing you every time they ask something.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while they're still talking. Write the question down, finish the call, then ring me. We'll work it out together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me sort our letters before the removal van comes. Keep them in date order, please; we shouldn't decide from a random handful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You kept them. I thought you'd want the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We wrote them over ten years. I need your choices, not permission to take the box. Start with the first envelope, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box. I just can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then seal it for the move and choose a day we'll open it together. Put both our names on it, please. I won't have you doing all this alone either.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For your sister's wedding, am I booking one room or two? I need the details correct before I confirm anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One is cheaper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the price settled, not the bed arrangement. Double or twins, please?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Twins. I don't want to confuse things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twins, then. I'll confirm breakfast separately: a place with your family, or should I meet you afterward in the lobby? One arrangement, please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do I bring my own towel when I visit now? I'd rather pack correctly than improvise in your bathroom.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not just any towel, please. The guest one or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is still on the hook. I haven't moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After I use it, do I wash it and put it back on that hook, or leave it with the guest laundry? The after-use arrangement, please.

cards.title: Take My Side
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into your interpretation of a conflict involving a shared relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're Alex's friend too. Explain that alternating allotment weekends is a fair rota, please, not me abandoning him.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We agreed all three of us would go every Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's attendance, not a division of work. Show him the covered weekends first; nobody's plot is being left untouched.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll talk to him, but you have to admit you changed the agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will. Say I changed it to keep us from resenting every Saturday together. 'Changed,' please, not 'walked out.' He needs to hear the difference.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When Mum asks about the holiday argument, lead with my offer to drive. Give her the solution before the complications.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: After you lost the tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, that's the cause. Put it after the recovery plan, please; otherwise you're giving her a problem with no answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm telling the whole story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All of it, certainly. Tell her I offered to drive us, then explain the lost tickets. In that order, please.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Prove We’re Close
cards.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to the reunion holding my hand. We'll make one clear entrance; no separate arrivals for people to misread.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They still think we're just friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll handle the introduction. Your name first, then 'my partner.' We don't leave that information to guesses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time someone asked, you let go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're right. This time I'll say it before anyone asks. Keep hold while I introduce you, please; I want us to get through the whole sentence together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send the sentence you deleted, not another 'fine.' Complete wording, please; I want to know what you're trusting me with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it sounds needy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then leave the need in. Don't edit out the part I need to answer. Send it to me as you wrote it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You first. You always sound so casual.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I check for your reply before I get out of bed. No 'just checking,' no smiley face. Now send me your sentence without apologising for it.
